findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The headline counts in verify.md match the attached logs: 718 files, 11,624 passed and 14 skipped; 13 files and 81 tests in the release suite; 3 files and 15/15 in the targeted run. The review ID, model and cross-agent status also match code-review.json. However, the build output in the attached logs shows that the full-suite and targeted runs did not build the same thing as the final release run. Their bundle chunk names and sizes differ. Most likely the full and targeted runs used the earlier borrowed-symlink dependencies, not the final frozen-lockfile install. verify.md still states the full-suite PASS for candidate `d2100c869` without that caveat. So the claim says more than the evidence proves.

The full-suite and targeted proof does not cover the candidate that was actually built. full-cli.log (14:17) and targeted.log (14:15) produce identical bundles, for example `chunk-VLMFVO5V.js` at 548.53 KB, `chunk-EDOIQXCR.js` at 54.72 KB, and `plan-approval-LETHWJPG.js`. release.log (14:32) produces different content-hashed chunks with different sizes, for example `chunk-4U4WATAT.js` at 548.46 KB, `chunk-67HZPHBD.js` at 54.19 KB, and `plan-approval-C45PB5AK.js`. tsup chunk names come from the file contents, so the code under test changed between those runs. This fits verify.md's own account that the dependency setup moved from borrowed symlinks to a frozen-lockfile install before the first release run, which then forced the regenerated bundles in `d2100c869`. Yet the checklist reports 'Test Suite: PASS — full CLI package: 11,624 passed' and 'Gherkin: PASS' against `d2100c869`, and the archive note calls these the 'final full/release logs'. A reader would conclude that the full package suite and the 15/15 targeted run passed on the candidate's actual dependency tree, but the logs show otherwise. Either re-run the full CLI suite and the targeted three-file run on the final frozen-lockfile tree at `d2100c869` and attach those logs, or say explicitly that those passes came from the pre-install dependency setup and only the 81-test release suite ran on the final build.

None of the attached logs records a commit SHA or a clean-tree check. All three runs come from `/private/tmp/safeword-4200-main-evidence/packages/cli`, a path whose name suggests a main checkout. The release log also waited on a test lock owned by a different checkout (`/Users/alex/.codex/worktrees/ffcf/safeword`). Nothing in the evidence ties these logs to branch `codex/4200-completion-progress` at `d2100c869`. Consider printing `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` at the top of each evidence log.

The Gherkin item says PASS for the plain-language receipt scenario. Per verify.md, that pass depended on a separate manual build of relay and the collector that is not in this ticket's evidence logs. The earlier seven-file run, which failed that scenario, is cited but not attached here. Its location in the external archive is noted, but it cannot be checked from this packet.

The scope limits are stated carefully and correctly: this is a partial fix for #5766, does not complete epic #4200, is CLI-fixture proof only, and has no native Codex/Cursor credit. Failed and cancelled reviews are kept in the record. The warnings from review `13a94973` are carried forward accurately.
